text.title: Administrator's ledger against the manager's records
text.lede: Matching runs in passes, strictest first. Each row is one pass: the bars are the records still unmatched on each side when the pass began, and the grey part is what that pass paired off. The two sides close toward the middle like a zip, and what is left at the bottom is the real work.
text.chartTitle: What each pass matched, and what it left
text.chartSub: Transactions for March 2026. Select a pass to see its rule and examples.
text.unmatchedRule: No pass could pair these. Each one needs a person: a missing booking on the other side, a wrong security, or a trade cancelled on one side only.

groups.note: Both sides carry the same trade reference. Nothing else is needed to pair them; amounts are compared afterwards.

groups.key: Pass 2: same security, date and quantity
groups.note: No shared reference, so pair on security identifier, trade date and quantity together. Used where the manager’s system issues its own references.
Same security and quantity, with the date allowed to differ by one day and the amount by 0.01. Catches late bookings and rounding.
Several ledger records that add up to one manager record: a block trade the administrator booked per fund and the manager booked once.
